_schema.note: One record per team, 16 records. Field set frozen before profile writing. Source of truth for the WWC team pages; all views (spreadsheet, HTML table) are generated from this file and are disposable.
_schema.keys: code is the primary key (FIBA three-letter). schedule_key joins to sites/wwc/reference/wwc_schedule_2026.csv, which uses UPPERCASE full names, not codes. Both are needed; neither alone is sufficient.
_schema.sources: A LIST, not a single URL, following the hooks.json convention. Verbatim quotes are attached where the source stated a figure directly.
_schema.derived: appearances_count and best_finish derive from the editions array wherever editions is non-null. Where editions is null the stored summary is the fallback.
_schema.confidence: high = cross-validated across two independent sources. medium = single source. low = single source that conflicted with something else; re-check before publishing.
_schema.nulls: null = exists, not researched. [] = researched, genuinely none. Never write a profile claim off a null.
_schema.roster_rule: player_count > 12 means a pool regardless of how the source labels it. FIBA's own tracker mislabels several pools as final. Never write a squad claim off a pool roster without hedging.
_schema.wnba: current / former / drafted_only counts derive from the players array and are validated. roster_basis says what list the block was built from — 'proxy' means no squad has been announced and membership is inference, not fact.
_schema.validator: sites/wwc/validate_teams.py (to be written) - assert 16 records, unique codes, 4 per group, schedule_key matches the schedule CSV, roster.status in enum, editions ranks 1..16.

qualification_summary.note: Villeurbanne sent two rather than three because its six-team field contained both the host (Germany) and a continental champion (Nigeria). The five directly-qualified teams all played a qualifying tournament anyway, so route and city answer different questions.

_corrections.note: Facts that were wrong in v1.0.0 and are now fixed. Kept deliberately so they are not reintroduced.
_corrections.AUS.coach: Was 'Paul Goriss'. Correct: Sandy Brondello, Opals head coach since April 2017.
_corrections.HUN.coach: Was 'László Cziczás' (from a stale Wikipedia infobox). Correct: Péter Völgyi since 2025; Cziczás is an assistant.
_corrections.MLI.wwc_record: The round-1 team page prototype shows 1 appearance and '15th - 2010'. Correct: 2 appearances, best 11th in 2022.
_corrections.ITA.coach_confidence: Was low. Capobianco confirmed by the Italian federation, contracted through June 2027.
_corrections.HUN.wwc_editions: Fourth appearance was listed as 1990 on a Wikipedia-derived grid. Correct: 1986, from FIBA's Hungary History tab.
_corrections.BEL.coach.us_connection: Called Thibault the WNBA's all-time coaching wins leader. Cheryl Reeve passed him in 2026. A decaying superlative should never have been stored in a data field — the falsifiability rule now applies to us_connection.summary as well.
_corrections.MLI.coach: Named Hamchétou Maïga-Ba as head coach on wiki sourcing. No evidence supports it; withdrawn to null. Mali's coach is currently unknown.
_corrections.KOR.wwc_appearances_count: Was 16 with a null editions array, on the basis of FIBA's prose article. Correct: 17, from FIBA's Korea History tab, which also supplied every placing. FIBA's article and FIBA's data disagree; the data is right.

teams.name: Korea

us_connection.summary: No known US role. Domestic WKBL and youth-development background; previously coached Korea's U18/U19 teams.

sources.claim: Korea History tab shows PLAYED 17 with 17 listed editions, 1959 through 2022, and 2ND = 2

wwc_record.note: RESOLVED: 17 completed appearances, confirmed from FIBA's Korea History tab. Note that FIBA's own team-profile article contradicts its own data - the article says Korea 'debuted in 1964' and calls 2026 their '17th edition in a row', but the History table lists 1959 and totals 17 played. The table is the source of record here; the 2ND = 2 tile matching the 1967 and 1979 silvers is an internal check on it. Korea have therefore appeared at every edition since 1959, an unbroken run of 17 that 2026 extends to 18 - the longest active streak in the field, shared with nobody.

olympic_record.note: 1984 silver is high confidence, as is 2020 being the most recent appearance. Appearance count is medium and several individual placings (1988, 1996, 2008) could not be resolved — three sources gave three different answers for 1988.

teams.name: Belgium

coach.name: Mike Thibault

us_connection.summary: American, and a USA Basketball insider before he took this job: assistant coach for the United States at the 2008 and 2024 Olympics and at the 2006 and 2022 World Cups. Three-time WNBA Coach of the Year; won the 2019 WNBA title as Washington Mystics head coach, with Belgium's Emma Meesseman as Finals MVP. Left the WNBA after 2022, took the Belgium job in 2025, and won EuroBasket at the first attempt.

coach.note: The Thibault-Meesseman reunion is the strongest single WNBA hook in the field: he coached her to the 2019 WNBA title and she was Finals MVP. He is also an American coaching a rival by choice, three years after leaving the WNBA. NOTE: an earlier version of this record called him the WNBA's all-time coaching wins leader. Cheryl Reeve passed him in 2026. That claim was falsifiable by a game and should never have been stored — see the durability rule in the profile rules doc.

olympic_record.note: Lost the Paris 2024 bronze game to Australia.
